solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Swimmer covering bottom that's not sexy?

indicators.note: a thing that covers another wraps round it, so the swimmer's word goes outside

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer
the rump is the bottom or backside

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up a swimmer whose costume covers their behind and judges the look unalluring.
explanation.walkthrough: F(RUMP)ISH: the swimmer is an actual fish, not a person in a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Frumpish describes dowdy, unfashionable dress, the opposite of alluring; the question mark flags the loose paraphrase.

clue.text: Fancy European flag

parts.note: a fancy is a passing fad or whim
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Admiring an ornate flag of some European nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag is a verb here, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire and weaken, which is what something does as it gradually loses strength.

clue.text: Prudent new investor will welcome this

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the preceding word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A careful new investor will be glad of this.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising trend in prices or the market is what anyone holding shares hopes to see.

clue.text: A pagan god is among ones identified for worship?

definitions.text: A pagan god is among ones identified for worship?

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and the wild

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the following short word sits inside the word for ones

parts.note: them stands for the ones being referred to
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of whether a heathen deity counts among those picked out to be worshipped.
explanation.walkthrough: PAN + THE(IS)M. The whole clue doubles as a sketch of the belief: gods found among all things.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheism is the belief that the divine is identical with the universe and nature, so any being may be worshipped as god.

clue.text: Small, it's a bustling camp settlement

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: bustling means moving busily about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a camp is a group or side within a larger body

explanation.surface: A small, busy camp that has become a settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: Camp is not a tent site but a faction, as in the rival camps in a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfaction can mean the payment or settling of a debt or claim, so a settlement.

clue.text: Base coat for a skirting edge

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its border, so the first words surround the next

parts.note: per means for each, for a, as in 'ten pounds per head'
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Decorating advice: put an undercoat on the skirting board's edge first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirting' borrows the skirting board from the decorating scene but works as the wrap-around signal, and 'for a' is read as a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is the first layer of paint applied to prepare a surface for later coats.

clue.text: Get to lecture? No parking

indicators.note: no parking says the parking letter must be absent, so it is removed

parts.note: to preach is to lecture someone

explanation.surface: Getting to a lecture, only to find there is no parking.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the map symbol for parking, removed from PREACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to arrive there, to get to it.

clue.text: This cherry is extra large, see

parts.note: more means extra
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
lo is an old word meaning look, see

explanation.surface: Pointing out how unusually big a cherry is.
explanation.definitionFit: The morello is a dark, sour variety of cherry often used in cooking and jams.

clue.text: Rhubarb is dry but full of one's spit

indicators.note: something full of another holds it inside, so the dry word encloses one

parts.note: rhubarb and rot are both British slang for nonsense
taken as written
sere is a literary word for dry, withered
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Rhubarb that is dry but juicy enough to make you salivate.
explanation.walkthrough: SER(I)E: the 's attached to one simply reads 'one is' and joins to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a cooking device with a rotating spit on which meat is roasted.

clue.text: Trigger's memo about opening time

indicators.note: opening something lets another thing in, so the time word is split to take the memo inside

parts.note: a date is a time when something happens

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the memo word is read back to front

parts.note: a note is a memo

explanation.surface: Someone named Trigger has written a memo about an opening time.
explanation.walkthrough: Trigger's reads as 'Trigger is', so the definition is a verb, not a name; 'opening' looks like a noun but tells one word to split around another.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate is to set off an explosive, the same action as triggering a bomb or charge.

clue.text: Orange or rust?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a reddish-orange colour named after a root vegetable
second, playful meaning: split as two words, decay on a motor vehicle, corrosion of the bodywork

explanation.surface: A paint chart question: is this shade orange or rust?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as CAR ROT, the answer describes rust eating a vehicle; the question mark admits the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable's name serves as a colour word for a bright reddish orange, as in carrot-topped hair.

clue.text: Progressive rock from one of The Drifters?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally a stone that moves along by turning over
second meaning: a wanderer with no settled home, and also a member of a famous band

explanation.walkthrough: Progressive rock and The Drifters (an American vocal group) point to music, and the answer is also a member of a British band; but each part works as plain words.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone that rolls progresses literally, and the proverb's rolling stone is a person who drifts without settling.

clue.text: The devil, he helps me out, keeping one close

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so the rearranged letters hold the next words inside
out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words, to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one
to close a business is to stop it

explanation.surface: A tempter claims the devil is helping him out while keeping someone close by.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled HE HELPS ME becomes MEPH...HELES, with I STOP set in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephistopheles is the demon of the Faust legend, to whom Faust sells his soul, so a name for the devil.

clue.text: A modest bar's fancy dishes

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so these letters are rearranged into new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A humble pub serves surprisingly elaborate food.
explanation.walkthrough: Dishes is slang for attractive people, not plates of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal terms for very good-looking people, especially men someone fancies.

clue.text: Fantastic — two bones

parts.note: rad is slang for excellent, fantastic
II is the Roman numeral two

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at being given two bones, perhaps by a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone, and radii is its Latin plural, so more than one of these bones.

clue.text: Divide then bind an element in a different form

definitions.text: an element in a different form

parts.note: to allot is to share out, divide up
to rope is to tie or bind

explanation.surface: Instructions to split something and then tie up a chemical element in an altered form.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotrope is one of the structurally distinct forms of a single chemical element, as diamond and graphite are of carbon.

clue.text: Sing, later playing percussion instruments

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with, arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Musicians are told to sing afterwards and play percussion meanwhile.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a steel rod bent into a three-sided shape and struck with a beater, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Zombie relative almost eating fruit

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside, so the shortened relative surrounds the fruit
almost means not quite all, so the relative's word loses its last letter

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
a tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: A horror scene: a zombie relative that is very nearly eating fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Zombie looks like a describing word for the relative, but it is the definition; the tomato counts as a fruit botanically.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone acting mechanically, without thought or will, like a robot.

clue.text: Half of them should care

indicators.note: half of means only the first two of the four letters are used

parts.note: the opening half of the word them
ought means should

explanation.surface: Half of those people ought to show some concern.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought can mean consideration or concern for others, as in 'spare a thought', so care.

clue.text: Early morning, first pair of big feet

parts.note: 1 a.m. is early in the morning, with the 1 read as I

indicators.note: first pair means only the opening two letters of the following word are used

parts.note: the opening two letters of big

explanation.surface: Waking early in the morning to find the first two of someone's big feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 in 1 AM is read as the letter I, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambi is a plural of iamb, the metrical foot of one short then one long syllable, so poetic feet.

clue.text: Unexpected item in bagging area is paint (red)

indicators.note: bagging means putting into a bag, so the rearranged letters enclose the area letter
unexpected suggests things are not in their usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: The supermarket self-checkout's notorious complaint about an unexpected item in the bagging area.
explanation.walkthrough: MINI(A)TE. The surface quotes the self-service till's stock warning, familiar to UK shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: To miniate is to colour or paint with red lead or vermilion, as in illuminated manuscripts.

clue.text: A contamination, perhaps

parts.note: surface reading: an example of some kind of pollution or taint
setter's reading: A is a blood group, and its contamination is a toxic infection of the bloodstream

explanation.walkthrough: The capital A is not the article but a blood type, so contaminating type A is a case of septicaemia.
explanation.definitionFit: Septicaemia, a dangerous infection of the circulating blood, is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: A kind of column of wood or ice

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the answer is formed from the run of letters in the next words

parts.note: the letters running across letters 4-8 of 'wood or ice'

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of column is made of timber or frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is the simplest of the classical Greek architectural orders, with plain capitals, so a type of pillar.

clue.text: Very good deal rejected for this type of aircraft

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the deal word runs backwards

parts.note: a good deal, as in a great amount, is a lot

explanation.surface: A very attractive offer is turned down for a particular kind of plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like a bargain, but it means a large amount.
explanation.definitionFit: VTOL stands for vertical take-off and landing, a class of aircraft like the Harrier jump jet.

clue.text: Stories about good old monarch's fluffy cat

indicators.note: about means around, so the stories word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories about a person
G is the abbreviation for good
O is the abbreviation for old
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: Tales are told about a kindly old king and his fluffy pet cat.
explanation.walkthrough: AN(G O R)A: ana is a crossword favourite for a collection of sayings or stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angora is a breed of long-haired domestic cat named after Ankara in Turkey, so a fluffy feline.

clue.text: Boxing, not boxing book author

indicators.note: boxing here means putting in a box, enclosing, so the first word goes round the rest

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book
Edward Lear was the author of A Book of Nonsense

explanation.surface: A writer insists a book's author is not into boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word appears twice with two jobs: first the sport as definition, then the enclosing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The noble art (of self-defence) is an old-fashioned literary phrase for the sport of fighting with fists.

clue.text: Criticism surrounding husband's funny routine

indicators.note: surrounding means going round, so the criticism word encloses the husband's letter

parts.note: stick is informal British for harsh criticism, as in 'taking stick'
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A comedian's husband draws criticism for his comic act.
explanation.walkthrough: S(H)TICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Shtick, from Yiddish, is a performer's characteristic comic routine or gimmick.

clue.text: Go outside when he finds a beach relic

indicators.note: outside means placed around, so the first word wraps the next words

parts.note: goods that go well sell well
as means when, as in 'as he finds it', followed by he

explanation.surface: An instruction to step outside once he discovers something left on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: SE(AS HE)LL: the sense of go is that of goods being bought.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell washed up on the shore is the remains of a dead sea creature, a relic left on the sand.
